cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, from David, Israel's king. He looks back to when they said to him, 'Let us go to the house of the LORD.' You know that moment when somebody invites you somewhere and your FACE answers before your mouth does?

cards.question: When they invite David to go to the house of the LORD, David says he was ___.

cards.text: Then they've made it, and David says, 'Our feet are standing…' Must be NICE having feet, friend, when all I've got is a gold base and a mustache.

cards.question: David and the people with him have arrived. Where does David say their feet are standing?

answers.text: At the foot of Mount Sinai

cards.text: Then David starts describing the city itself, the way it's built. The man's standing in the gate and he's already a TOUR GUIDE.

cards.question: Standing in Jerusalem, David says it is built up as a city split apart.

cards.text: Jerusalem is where the tribes of the LORD go up, as a testimony for Israel. A group chat can argue for three DAYS over where to meet, and here come whole TRIBES headed for the same city.

cards.question: The tribes of the LORD go up to Jerusalem to give thanks to the name of the LORD.

cards.text: And Jerusalem is also where the thrones of judgment stand. Big decisions get made in this city, friend, and I can't even decide between sprinkles and chocolate chips without a long pause.

cards.question: David says the thrones of judgment in Jerusalem are the thrones of the house of ___.

cards.text: Then the tour guide stops pointing at buildings, and out comes an instruction. Lean in, friend, this one's a big one.

cards.question: David gives an instruction about Jerusalem. What does he say to pray for?

cards.text: And David even gives the words to pray, starting with who should prosper. Thank goodness, because left to me it'd just be, 'Uh… good stuff for Jerusalem… amen?'

cards.question: The prayer David gives asks for those who love Jerusalem to prosper.

cards.text: The prayer goes on: 'May there be peace within your walls, and prosperity inside your fortresses.' Friend, that's a prayer I'd frame and hang right over my ovens.

Then David says what he will say himself: 'Peace be within you.' Man, I could've used that line back in the junk drawer I spent years in, with the dead batteries arguing ALL night over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: David says he will say, Peace be within you. Why does he say he'll do it?

answers.text: For the sake of his brothers and friends
To win the favor of the crowds
Because the elders asked him to

cards.question: In the last line of the song, David says he will seek Jerusalem's prosperity for the sake of the ___ of the LORD our God.
